[ARTHUR LEIGH ALLEN]
Description: Arthur Leigh Allen, born December 18, 1933, was the primary suspect in the Zodiac Killer case, identified by Graysmith as the perpetrator in his investigation and by "Mike" as his shooter. He was widely believed to be the "Zodiac" killer.

Allen had a background as a Navy man and worked as a chemist, including at Union Oil in Pinole. He was also a former public school teacher, specifically at Valley Springs, but was fired from elementary schools for molesting children or touching kids. Notably, he was fired eight months before the first Vallejo murder. He was later arrested for molestation in January 1975.

Regarding his connection to the Zodiac case, Allen was interrogated by Inspectors Armstrong, Toschi, and Sergeant Mulanax, and his investigation was reopened by Sergeant Bawart. He denied involvement in the murders and provided explanations for incriminating statements and items. He was interviewed by Toschi on August 4, 1971, and also wrote a letter to Toschi. Allegations against him included discussing hunting people and using the name "Zodiac" in 1968.

Investigators conducted searches of his residence and basement (in 1991), and he was brought to the Hall of Justice for investigation. He was known to drive a white Kharmann Ghia. While he was noted to live in Vallejo at some point, his trailer was moved to Santa Rosa on August 7, 1971, indicating a later residence there.

Allen was described as being sick with diabetes and possibly ambidextrous. He died of a heart attack in 1992 before he could be arrested for the murders. DNA tests conducted on Zodiac envelopes did not match his DNA.
